@title BlobBatchAnchor
 @notice Independent real-blob anchor for the Hybrid TEE-Rollup revision branch.
         This contract deliberately does NOT modify BoundedTaskRollup or the project's
         main Hardhat config. It provides a separate, self-contained anchor that records,
         for a batch carried by a REAL EIP-4844 blob:
           * the current transaction's blob versioned hash, obtained via the BLOBHASH
             opcode (EIP-4844) at a NON-ZERO index,
           * the off-chain-computed payloadHash (keccak256 of the decoded batch content),
           * the taskCount,
           * the submitting block and address.
         Business semantics ("does payloadHash/taskCount actually correspond to the blob?")
         are intentionally NOT verified on-chain: the EVM cannot read blob bytes. They MUST
         be verified INDEPENDENTLY off-chain by fetching the blob from the beacon chain,
         decoding it with the revision codec, and recomputing keccak256(content) and
         taskCount, then comparing to the stored values. The verify script does exactly this.
         A distinct calldata-benchmark branch exists for gas comparison. It emits a
         DIFFERENT event (CalldataBatchAnchored) and NEVER sets blobVersionedHash, so a
         calldata payload can never be mistaken for, or impersonate, a real blob anchor.
         Overwrite protection: a given payloadHash may be anchored only once, and a given
         blob versioned hash may be used by at most one anchor. This prevents replay /
         collision / overwrite attacks where different content claims the same hash.
@notice Emitted only for a REAL blob anchor (blobhash opcode, non-zero index).

@notice Distinct tag for the calldata benchmark branch. MUST NOT be confused
         with a real blob anchor; blobVersionedHash is left zero.

@notice Benchmark branch: records the same commitment shape via calldata only.
         Emits CalldataBatchAnchored (different tag) and leaves blobVersionedHash zero.
@notice Bounded deterministic-task experiment, not a general VM or AI fault proof.

@notice TEST-ONLY helper contract for evm/revision/security.test.js.
         It is NOT part of the production system. On receiving ETH it tries to
         re-enter `rollup.withdraw(address(this))` to prove the rollup's
         reentrancy guard prevents a malicious recipient from extracting more
         than the single owed amount. The re-entered call must revert.

         any inbound ETH transfer so the `withdraw` failure path (recipient
         that rejects payment) can be exercised by the security suite.

Emits CalldataBatchAnchored (different tag) and leaves blobVersionedHash zero."}},"notice":"Independent real-blob anchor for the Hybrid TEE-Rollup revision branch.         This contract deliberately does NOT modify BoundedTaskRollup or the project's         main Hardhat config. It provides a separate, self-contained anchor that records,         for a batch carried by a REAL EIP-4844 blob:           * the current transaction's blob versioned hash, obtained via the BLOBHASH             opcode (EIP-4844) at a NON-ZERO index,           * the off-chain-computed payloadHash (keccak256 of the decoded batch content),           * the taskCount,           * the submitting block and address.         Business semantics (\"does payloadHash/taskCount actually correspond to the blob?\")         are intentionally NOT verified on-chain: the EVM cannot read blob bytes. They MUST         be verified INDEPENDENTLY off-chain by fetching the blob from the beacon chain,         decoding it with the revision codec, and recomputing keccak256(content) and         taskCount, then comparing to the stored values. The verify script does exactly this.         A distinct calldata-benchmark branch exists for gas comparison. It emits a         DIFFERENT event (CalldataBatchAnchored) and NEVER sets blobVersionedHash, so a         calldata payload can never be mistaken for, or impersonate, a real blob anchor.         Overwrite protection: a given payloadHash may be anchored only once, and a given         blob versioned hash may be used by at most one anchor.
